items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-12-30
items.q: I never did get your boy's name Chauncey Highland... I'd never seen his name written on him. I didn't know how to spell it on him.

ctx.x: Well now, if you would compile it from 1941, you would see it goes over the 30. Yeah. With the break in between for the nightclub operation and for the New Orleans Post Office, they've not got four years that are not counted. Yeah. Not four. The Post Office counts because it's Civil Service. So that's why today I have twenty-six years instead of thirty or thirty-one.

So you've had a couple of breaks in there. That's right. I see. You know, I never did get your boy's name Chauncey Highland. Chauncey Highland. How do you spell it? Biggest crook you've ever seen. S-Y-L-E-N-D. H?
Y-L-E-N-D. Yeah. I'd never seen his name written on him. I didn't know how to spell it on him. Right. Well, he confidants Beansy.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: And then the next biggest crook was this one that I picked up here, Chauncey Highland, on the revision of my band.

ctx.x: Yeah, you would deal with one man?

One man. How much territory? The man that first picked me up was Bernard Galway. And I had him, not only was his name, but Rabinowitz. And then finally this Al Travis that was the biggest crook in the world. And then the next biggest crook was this one that I picked up here, Chauncey Highland, on the revision of my band. Those were crooks. They weren't under bondage like the big companies are now. And the only major company that I went with that was under bonds was when I went to Joe Glazer. See, Glazer wanted me…
